name: Big Stamp
generated_description:
At 5,377 feet, Big Stamp is a summit in Tennessee. The Big Stamp Trail covers 0.2 miles round trip (out-and-back) with about 59 feet of elevation gain — a gradual walk with modest climbing.

The Route

Along the way the route passes a hut (Bald Mountain Shelter) near mile 0.17 — useful checkpoints for judging your pace.

Getting There

The trailhead is at 35.99825, -82.47597 (tap for driving directions). It's roughly 30 miles north of Asheville, North Carolina. Arrive early on weekends — trailhead lots at popular peaks fill quickly, and cell service is often unreliable once you leave the highway.

When to Go

Late May through October is the main season. Snow and ice linger into spring and return early in fall at this latitude and elevation; in winter this becomes a different, more serious undertaking requiring traction devices and warm layers.

Know Before You Go

Most hikers should budget about 0.5 hours of moving time; add margin for breaks, photos and the descent. Download the GPX track from this page before you go — cell coverage is unreliable in the mountains and a saved route works offline in any GPS app. Conditions change: verify current access, closures and weather with the official land manager before you go. Trail data is sourced from OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL).

Looking to link objectives or plan a weekend? Nearby summits include Beartown Mountain, Jane Bald and Mount Cammerer — each has its own guide on this site.
